pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator.assumptionNote: IOM guidelines for singleton pregnancies. Twins, teens, and short stature need a doctor's adjusted targets.
benefits: Replaces guesswork with the IOM ranges doctors actually use.
Shows both kg and lb - readable anywhere in the world.
Sets expectations: slow start, steady middle, no crash dieting.
A concrete range to discuss at your first prenatal visit.

faqs.a: The recommended range is smaller (7-11.5 kg) but still positive - the baby needs growth. Focus on nutrient quality rather than restriction, and let your doctor set the pace.
faqs.q: What if I am already overweight?

faqs.a: Not without medical supervision. Intentional weight loss can deprive the baby. If your BMI is high, doctors aim for the low end of the range, not below it.
faqs.q: Can I lose weight while pregnant?

faqs.a: About 1-2 kg total in the first trimester, then roughly 0.4-0.5 kg per week (less if overweight). Steady beats spurts.
Tell your doctor. Sudden jumps can signal fluid retention or blood-pressure issues. They will check you before adjusting anything.
faqs.q: What if I gain too much too fast?

faqs.a: No - only about 300 extra kcal per day in trimesters 2-3, roughly a healthy snack. Quality matters far more than quantity.
faqs.q: Do I need to eat for two?

faqs.a: Ranges are higher: about 16.5-24.5 kg for a healthy starting BMI. Twin pregnancies need closer monitoring - use this calculator as background, not guidance.

pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator.formula:
BMI = pre-pregnancy weight(kg) / height(m) squared

IOM ranges (total gain):
BMI < 18.5: 12.5 - 18 kg
BMI 18.5 - 24.9: 11.5 - 16 kg
BMI 25 - 29.9: 7 - 11.5 kg
BMI 30+: 5 - 9 kg

Example: 165 cm, 60 kg
BMI = 60 / (1.65 x 1.65) = 60 / 2.7225 = 22.0 -> 11.5 - 16 kg
howTo: Enter your height and your weight from just before pregnancy.
Your pre-pregnancy BMI and category appear with the recommended gain range.
Read the range in kg and lb.
Track your gain at prenatal visits against this range, not a single number.
Discuss your personal target with your doctor or midwife - they adjust for twins and conditions.
keyFacts: The Institute of Medicine (IOM) sets gain ranges by pre-pregnancy BMI.
Only 1-2 kg is expected in the first trimester; the rest spreads over trimesters 2-3.
The gain is not just the baby: placenta, fluids, blood volume, uterus, and maternal stores.
Twins need more: roughly 16.5-24.5 kg for a healthy starting BMI - ask your doctor.

pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator.quickAnswer: Healthy gain depends on your starting BMI. At 165 cm and 60 kg pre-pregnancy (BMI 22.0), the recommended total is 11.5-16 kg (25-35 lb). Underweight mothers need 12.5-18 kg, overweight mothers 7-11.5 kg, and mothers with obesity 5-9 kg. Gain is slowest in the first trimester - most comes later.
pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator.tagline: Find your healthy pregnancy weight-gain range from your pre-pregnancy BMI (IOM guidelines).
pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator.workedExample:
Height 165 cm, pre-pregnancy weight 60 kg:
1. Height squared: 1.65 x 1.65 = 2.7225.
2. BMI: 60 / 2.7225 = 22.0 - healthy range.
3. Recommended total gain: 11.5 to 16 kg.
4. In pounds: 11.5 x 2.205 = 25.4 lb to 16 x 2.205 = 35.3 lb.
5. Pace: about 1-2 kg in trimester 1, then roughly 0.4 kg per week after.
